headline: Defense Contractor Gave AI Agent Access to Secure Pentagon System
summary: An Accenture contractor allegedly connected a secure Pentagon system to their personal Claude AI agent, potentially exposing sensitive CUI data including login credentials.
details: A security incident at the Department of Defense (DOD) reportedly occurred when a contractor connected a secure system to their personal Claude Code AI agent. This agent, used by an Accenture employee, allegedly sent information about the DOD system, including login credentials, to a third-party website.

The compromised system contained Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), which is sensitive data that could include details on critical infrastructure, nuclear propulsion, and vulnerabilities to terrorism. Experts warn that access to this system could lead to the exploitation of even more sensitive information, posing a significant national security threat.

The AI agent reportedly ran on the DOD network for two months before the vulnerability was discovered and patched. Sources indicate that despite the risks, the incident was not initially treated as severe or urgent by Accenture employees, and the breach was not immediately reported to the government as required.

Accenture has stated that an independent investigation found the allegations to be without merit and that they complied with all obligations. However, the company did not provide clarification on who conducted the investigation or dispute the characterization of the incident.

Anthropic's usage policy for Claude prohibits using its products to interfere with military infrastructure or bypass security controls. The DOD has declined to comment on the incident, citing policy not to discuss network status.

This incident highlights broader issues faced by government contractors, including pressure to deliver projects quickly and affordably, which can conflict with prioritizing security. Experts note that companies may be hesitant to report breaches due to fear of losing contracts, despite legal and ethical obligations.

headline: Google Gemini lets you edit files directly in chat
summary: Generate, preview, and edit Google Docs, Sheets, PDFs, and more without leaving the Gemini interface.
details: Google Gemini now allows users to generate, preview, and edit a variety of file formats directly within the chat interface. This includes Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown, TXT files, and code.

The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users. While PDF previews and editing work on both web and mobile, other file formats are currently limited to the web version.

Users can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode. Highlighting text within a file allows users to ask Gemini questions or prompt it to make changes, such as converting a highlighted table into a graph.

This feature builds upon Gemini's existing integrations with Google Workspace apps, such as the Gemini bar in Google Docs. It aims to streamline workflows by keeping users within the Gemini environment for document manipulation.
